facts.value: There are four different Economic English courses (A-B-C-D) as part of the elective modules for Economic English. All courses are offered simultaneously each semester.
All elective module courses have the same level of difficulty (Target level C1.1 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages).
The paid course 'Economic English “Higher”' is very suitable as preparation for the elective courses.
Preliminary admission for the qualification section of the Bachelor's examination in accordance with §9 paragraph 5.
There is a two-stage registration procedure with different deadlines. Both stages must be completed and the Online Qualifying Test must be passed.
Stage 1: Registration period: September 21, 2026 – October 5, 2026 via QIS.
Stage 2: Examination registration and cancellation period: October 8, 2026 – October 21, 2026 via QIS.

The successful completion of a qualifying test at CEFR level B2.2, held at the beginning of each semester, is required unless a Bachelor's elective module course in Economic English has already been successfully completed.

Exceptions: Students with the Cambridge Certificate C1, a score of at least 100 points in the TOEFL test, or a score of at least 7.5 in the IELTS test must upload this language proof in PDF format during the Online Qualifying Test on September 28, 2026.
Elective Module Course A: Current Global Economic Affairs
Monetary and Financial Policy, Energy Policy, Global Trade, Migration and Labor Markets.
Joanne Glen, Guojun Wong, Barry Hawthorne.
Group 1: Mondays 14:00 – 16:00, starts October 12, 2026. Group 2: Tuesdays 12:00 – 14:00, starts October 13, 2026. Group 3: Thursdays 10:00 – 12:00, starts October 15, 2026.
Elective Module Course B: Marketing
Marketing Mix, Behavioral Economics and Consumer Behavior, Digital Marketing, Gender, Ethnicity and Marketing, Artificial Intelligence, Sustainability and Ethical Marketing, Political Marketing.
Caroline Pung.
Wednesdays 14:00 – 16:00, starts October 14, 2026.
Elective Module Course C: The Entrepreneur
The Entrepreneur and Entrepreneurship, Market Research and Feasibility Analysis, Strategy and Pricing, Marketing and Branding, Financial Forecasts and Financing.
Barry Hawthorne.
Tuesdays 10:00 – 12:00, starts October 13, 2026.
Elective Module Course D: Banking & Finance Topics

Alternative Finance: Crowdfunding / Shadow Banking / Complementary Currencies, Fintech: Cryptocurrencies / Cashless Societies / Fintech Startups, Ethical/ Social Banking: Islamic Banking / Microfinance / Climate & Capitalism, Topics of Current Interest: Stock Market Crisis / Zombie Companies / Trade Wars.
Caroline Pung.
Tuesdays 16:00 – 18:00, starts October 13, 2026.
All participants receive 6 credit points for the successful completion of an elective Economic English course: English for Economists.
An internal C1.1 certificate will be issued for the successfully completed course.
